brief: Goldman Sachs Global Views: 2026 growth tracked potential as fiscal easing and the AI boom offset drags from the Iran war and tariffs. The 2027 base case repeats this as falling energy prices offset fading fiscal and AI tailwinds, but risks skew down. The immediate risk is energy, near March/April highs on Middle East escalation fears. Sustained higher DM long yields could cut GDP 0.6%, and AI's consumer wealth boost fades, faster if AI stocks keep falling. Central banks still hike near term, Fed in December to 4 to 4.25%, ECB in December to 2.75%, BOE to 4%, but GS's strongest view is that central banks deliver fewer hikes than priced, so cross asset strategists favor the recent rally extending, caution momentum amid narrow breadth, and see the S&P resuming its climb post midterms. Separately, GS's Brazil desk runs light risk into fiscal reform signals and a possible orthodox cabinet appointment. RBNZ is now seen hiking twice to a 3.25% terminal rate. Hyperscaler earnings this week test the AI spending cycle after Meta raised capex guidance and turned free cash flow negative.
